title: yadgar/iam
$comment: Closure is PER CHART (ADR-0850): this file closes the key set this chart owns and nothing upstream or downstream of it. `additionalProperties: false` sits at the root and at every declared block, so a misspelled key anywhere in the tree is refused by name instead of silently dropped or silently accepted. OPEN (no `properties`, no closure): `global`, because helm injects it into every subchart and the parent owns its closure; this chart reads only `global.hostname`, through `templates/_hostname.tpl` (`.context.Values.global`, ADR-0808); `resources` and `rollingUpdate`, because the shape they take is the Kubernetes API's and this chart only forwards it through `toYaml`/`with`. EXTRAS (leaves `chart/values.yaml` never states, read straight off the templates): `image.digest`, rewritten at package time by ci-release (D65), read in `templates/deployment.yaml`; `networkPolicy.scrapeFrom.namespace`, read in `templates/networkpolicy.yaml`, with `values.yaml` shipping the parent block `scrapeFrom: {}` empty; `tls.clientCaSecret` and `tls.clientCaSecretKey` (B-U5E expand, kept by B-U5: `templates/deployment.yaml` renders the CA env, mount and volume only when `tls.enabled` is true and `clientCaSecret` names a Secret); `nats.tls.enabled` (B-N3E, the K-8 expand for the broker hop, ADR-0852: `templates/deployment.yaml` renders `NATS_TLS_ENABLED` only when it is present, `templates/render-checks.yaml` refuses `true`, and the binary does not read it until B-N3 makes it required). Types, toggle shapes and `required` are NOT this file's job (ADR-0847): `render-checks.yaml` owns them, and `autoscaling`/`autoscaling.enabled`'s `kindIs` guards (ledger 1135) are the worked example — a schema `type` on either would refuse the chart's own default render the day the value changed shape, which is why every leaf here is `{}`. Four exceptions. `nats.tls` and `nats.tls.enabled` (B-N3E) carry `type: object` and `type: boolean` with NO `required`, the shape gateway#104 ruled for both repos: a null, a quoted string or a non-map is refused by the schema, and the key stays optional until B-N3. `tls.enabled` and `iamDb.tls.enabled` (ADR-0845, C-SVb) keep `type: boolean` and their parent blocks keep `required: [enabled]`: `required` alone passes a null value through, so the leaf needs its type too (K-1) — `templates/render-checks.yaml` still carries the `hasKey`/`kindIs` guard that produces ADR-0845's own named sentence, because a schema refusal and a render-check refusal report differently and both are asserted. `tls.clientAuth` (B-U5, ADR-0854 extending ADR-0845) carries `type: string` and the `enum` `off`/`optional`/`required`, and `tls.required` lists it: the binary refuses an absent `LISTEN_TLS_CLIENT_AUTH`, so the chart has no default for it and refuses a missing, unquoted (`off` read as false) or unknown value at the schema; `templates/render-checks.yaml` keeps the guard and adds the two cross-key refusals a schema cannot state (a verifying mode with `tls.enabled` false, or with no `tls.clientCaSecret`).
